issues.legal_issue: A female Hindu who already held a property right and possessed the property when the succession reform law commenced became its full owner when a partition allotted her share, even where the partition award described her interest as a limited estate.
material_facts: The widow inherited an interest in her husband's property under the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937, and had a pre-existing right to a share.
Before the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 commenced, an arbitration award partitioned the property and allotted her specific properties; the award was made a decree.
The award described her interest in the allotted properties as a widow's estate and provided for her physical or constructive possession.
A suit sought to restrain her from alienating the properties on the ground that she remained a limited owner.
issues.conclusion: The widow became the full owner of the allotted properties under section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956. Section 14(2) did not apply because the award separated property to which she already had a pre-existing right. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1), including its Explanation, gives the widest meaning to possession and acquisition: possession may be actual or constructive, and property may be acquired in any manner, including inheritance or partition. Section 14(2) is an exception to section 14(1), applying when an instrument, decree, order, or award creates an acquisition for the first time without a pre-existing right. The Court applied sections 3(1)–(3) of the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937, and followed Gummalapura Taggina Matada Kotturuswami v. Setra Veerayya, [1959] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 968; S.S. Munnalal v. S.S. Rajkumar, [1962] Supp. 3 S.C.R. 418; and Sukhram v. Gauri Shankar, [1968] 1 S.C.R. 476. It also referred to Rangaswami Naicker v. Chinnammal, A.I.R. 1964 Mad. 387, on the purpose of section 14.

rule.if: female_hindu_property_status_case and preexisting_property_right and possessed_when_reform_law_commenced and partition_allocated_existing_share and award_prescribed_limited_estate

predicates.female_hindu_property_status_case: The proceeding concerns whether a female Hindu holds property as a limited or full owner under a succession reform law.
predicates.preexisting_property_right: The female Hindu already had a legal right to the property before the instrument or proceeding that allocated her specific share.
predicates.possessed_when_reform_law_commenced: The female Hindu held the property, actually or constructively in a manner recognized by law, when the reform law commenced.
predicates.partition_allocated_existing_share: A partition separated and allotted to the female Hindu property representing her existing share.
predicates.award_prescribed_limited_estate: The award that allotted the property described her interest as a limited estate.
predicates.became_full_owner: The female Hindu held the allotted property as its full owner.

issues.definition: When a female Hindu in a property-status proceeding had a pre-existing right, possessed the property when the reform law commenced, and received her existing share through a partition award describing a limited estate, she became its full owner.
